case_title: NAGABHUSHAN v. THE STATE OF KARNA TAKA
aggravating_circumstances: Setting fire to the victim with kerosene, intent to cause death
neutral_facts: The accused, who was married to the deceased, poured kerosene on her and set her ablaze with a matchstick, resulting in her death. The deceased provided two dying declarations, one of which was corroborated by medical evidence and the absence of a stove at the scene. The accused claimed the fire was accidental, but the High Court found this defense unsupported. The trial court initially acquitted the accused, but the High Court reversed this decision, finding the evidence against the accused sufficient to convict him under Section 302 IPC for murder.
